D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Two page-creation tools are documented. Tool annotations such as readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint are not published in the official tutorial. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter, preview flow, elicitation, or approval workflow is documented. 3. Authorization uses a Bearer API key. The general API-key guide describes read-only, read-write, and admin permission levels; MCP inheritance and key revocation details are not specified. 4. Separate development and production endpoints are documented. No read-only MCP endpoint, toolset filter, or query-free mode is documented. 5. The MCP tutorial does not specify PII masking or data-scope boundaries. 6. General API docs state requests are rate limited and describe HTTP 429 responses, without a numeric limit; recipe links default to 30 days expiry, maximum 365 days. No MCP result cap is published. 7. The API references document request validation errors, including invalid filters, invalid measurement quantities, and mutually exclusive product_ids/upcs. MCP-specific coercion or parameter overrides are not documented. 8. MCP logging, audit trail, telemetry, and opt-out behavior are not documented. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, report, or upsell tool is named in the official list. 10. The tutorial says agents can use natural language and MCP formats API inputs; no server-provided skills or initialize instructions are published. 11. No cross-call memory or state behavior is documented. 12. The tutorial documents development and production endpoints with the same two operations; no sub-server hierarchy is described. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script, or unrestricted request tool is listed.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official MCP tutorial lists two tools and describes both: create-recipe and create-shopping-list. No official total beyond those two is stated. The APIs.io third-party page independently names the same two tools and reports an anonymous tools/list capture, but its available page copy does not expose the schemas. Other catalogues describe the separate fig-mcp.instacart.com consumer connector; those tools are not added to this endpoint’s list.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim complete initialize and tools/list definitions were available. The third-party APIs.io page gives a token estimate based on its own capture, which is not used.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The public API documents additional operations beyond the two MCP tools, including finding nearby retailers and retailer/location functions; these are not listed as tools in the official MCP tutorial. End users can select a store, add matched ingredients or products to a cart, and check out from the generated Instacart-hosted page. The MCP tools create links to those pages rather than performing checkout.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official tutorial recommends using natural language to call the tools and says MCP handles API formatting; it does not document server-side enforcement of agent behavior. The recipe API reference recommends caching generated URLs and reusing them unless the recipe changes, and says only supported measurement units should be passed.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The general API overview says API communications use HTTPS and that rate limiting protects the system against misuse. No MCP-specific data retention, AI training, audit, or privacy promise was found in the tutorial.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The tutorial describes creating shoppable recipe and shopping-list pages whose links let users select a store, add items, and check out.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The API reference documents input validation and expiry behavior for the linked page operations. The tutorial’s natural-language and URL-caching guidance is not described as server-enforced. No MCP-specific logging, privacy filtering, or confirmation mechanism is documented.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint-existence evidence reports HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC response, while the supplied pre-fetched anonymous POST to https://mcp.instacart.com/mcp returned HTTP 500 with a TypeError and no accompanying WWW-Authenticate header. The differing outcomes may reflect different request payloads; the successful test payload was not provided.

The third-party listing for https://fig-mcp.instacart.com/mcp describes OAuth and tools cart and search_products, while the official Developer Platform tutorial documents https://mcp.instacart.com/mcp with API-key Bearer authentication and tools create-recipe and create-shopping-list. These are different endpoint paths and are not combined.
observations_for_research: The documented MCP operations create shoppable landing pages; end-user store selection and checkout occur after opening the generated link.
Development and production endpoints are separated by environment, while the documented tool names are shared.
The official MCP documentation links each tool to a Developer Platform API reference, but does not reproduce the MCP input schemas.
notes: Checked supplied links.json, links_check.txt, pages/INDEX.txt, captured official documentation pages and scripts, and the local code folder; no official source repository was listed or cloned. The two linked API reference pages were used for operation behavior and validation, not treated as MCP schemas. The supplied OAuth metadata probes were used as provided. Unofficial or third-party directory material about the fig-mcp.instacart.com consumer connector was treated as a separate endpoint, not evidence for the input endpoint. No MCP-specific pricing or privacy terms were found in the supplied official evidence.
